review: [zoya · changes] Verdict: changes (4 must-fix, rest minor). Structure is right: five beats map 1:1 to console sections and TERMS wording is mostly used (suspend, lineage hold, record, dry-run diff, residual damage R / collateral loss C, root candidates). MUST-FIX: (1) Pacing: nothing lets the presenter hold beats 1-3 live. 'ks run' is a seeded batch; 'ks contain' needs a live gateway but a finished run gives IO; --hold is the hold window, not a pause. Add a tick pacing/step option (e.g. --tick-ms or --pause-at SEQ) or state that Break/Identify/Contain are shown from a completed run via 'ks console --html', and pick one. (2) Terms: ADR splits 'inject' (fault only) from '--rogue', but TERMS defines inject as fault OR arbitrary code in the rogue agent, and SEC-02 §3 shows 'ks run --rogue ... [--inject F2+]' while ADR uses '--fault F2+'. Align TERMS and SEC-02 §3 to the ADR flags (I will update TERMS inject row) so jury docs match the CLI. (3) 'console' means two things: a read-only page that never imports signer code, and the 'ks.console' signer that is the only one allowed to revoke. Jury will ask 'so the console can revoke?'. Rename the signer identity (e.g. ks.operator) or add one sentence. (4) Beat 4 promises scorecard vs snapshot and revert-culprit-only baselines, but the console reads only the run dir and score.json (ADR-06 keys); say where baseline numbers live in the run dir or that 'ks bench' output is embedded, else we cannot show them. MINOR: 'escaped payment' (beat 4) is a banned synonym; use 'irreversible tainted effect released' / 'released payment'. 'independents' -> 'independent agents'. 'ks blame' introduces an unlocked word (TERMS bans 'blame result'); keep the command but on screen and in narration say 'root candidates', add 'blame' as command alias in TERMS. 'incident console' not in TERMS; I will add it. Audit beat: console embeds a build-time verify, so after the jury edits a record line the page is stale until 'ks console --html' is rerun; say so, and show 'ks verify RUN' (exit TAMPER, first bad seq) as the live proof. TERMS uses 'first bad index'; pick seq or index once. Rehearse editing a line before the last witnessed seq, since edits after it are not detected. Typing risk in Recover: 'ks recover --apply PLAN_ID --approve ITEM' needs ids copied from output; make --dry-run print the exact apply command ready to paste. Time budget otherwise fits: about 9 commands across 5 min is workable if scripted. Word count 899 of 900, so edits must be swaps, not additions.
